brief: US equities fell as September core CPI ran hot (0.3% m/m vs 0.2% consensus, annual core at 2.6%, supercore the hottest since January), pushing Fed hike odds for October toward 60% right after the release from about 20% pre-release, before intraday odds pared back to 32% as the AI trade sold off: the S&P 500 snapped a 53-day streak without a 1% decline and the SOX fell 10% in six sessions amid scrutiny of CoreWeave's debt yield. Bank earnings were mixed, with BofA and Morgan Stanley FICC hit by the rate surge but offset by AI-financing tailwinds. Oil rose on Houthi strikes on Aramco's headquarters and Iranian threats to close the Strait of Hormuz, despite ample Saudi and Iraqi supply. In Europe, ASML raised FY26 guidance but warned capacity cannot meet 2027-28 AI demand; French yields stayed elevated as Lagarde pushed fiscal responsibility back onto Paris, while BoE's Pill's hike skepticism lifted UK housebuilders. In Asia, China's exports surged 36.3% y/y toward a $1T surplus on AI-related shipments as inflation firmed, Singapore's MAS held policy steady, the BOJ leaned against an October hike, and BofA's Asia survey showed rising AI-monetization conviction.
